display: Small-batch rose-water distiller in Nairobi, a former chemistry teacher.

signals.text: I'm looking for clean roses to distil, ideally from a grower who can tell me what was sprayed and when.
Market roses keep coming in with a faint chemical smell. I threw out a whole 40-litre batch of petals this month and won't sell anything I can't trust.
My still only runs about two days a week because clean petals are scarce. Demand isn't the problem.
I have eleven 250ml bottles left and regular customers are waiting for the next batch.
On 10 October I'm testing two new stalls at Wakulima market, and I'd like a cheap way to check petals for spray residue before I commit to one.
I keep a notebook of which stall, which day and how the petals felt. I want to turn it into a proper supplier record, but I don't know any grower who keeps spray records.
I'd like to find a grower in Kenya who would sell petals for hydrosol rather than cut-flower export.
I've been thinking about how chemistry is taught in English to children who think in Kikuyu, and I'd like to see science taught in the mother tongue.
When a batch fails, money gets tight, because my working capital is small and I can't absorb many losses.
I'm worn down by a slow family legal matter that keeps getting postponed, and I'm trying to keep it out of my work.
Sometimes I worry that a business this small doesn't matter, and I want to see that a careful craft product can find its place.

offers.text: Hand-bottled small-batch rose water. I check pH, colour and smell on every batch and reject what fails.
Sixteen years of teaching secondary-school chemistry. I can explain concepts clearly to teenagers and adults.
Distillation know-how: temperature control, cut points, and hydrosol quality checks.
A 200-litre stainless steel steam still I built to my own spec. I can advise on building, gaskets, condenser problems and upkeep for small stills.
About forty regular buyers in Nairobi who value quality, including a spa owner. This is a channel for clean, hand-made botanical products.
A simple batch-QC routine (pH meter, glassware, sensory check) that other small producers can copy.
A notebook of petal quality by stall and date at Wakulima market, which I can share as a record of what that market actually delivers.
Weekend football coaching for under-14s, with a focus on keeping training fun and fair.

catchers.hypo: I grow roses outside the export chain and don't spray weekly. I keep a spray log and I'm looking for someone who wants petals.
catchers.can: Buy petals for a trial batch, give feedback on smell and yield, and become a regular buyer if the batches pass my checks.
catchers.confirm: Can you tell me, for each harvest, what was sprayed on the roses and when?

catchers.hypo: I work with flower farms near Naivasha and Limuru and know growers with older rose beds. Would an introduction help you?
catchers.can: Ask Mary, Grace's cousin who works in horticulture, to introduce unsprayed or low-spray growers. I'd go and test their petals myself.
catchers.confirm: Are you talking about roses grown for petals, not cut-flower stems treated for vase life?

catchers.hypo: I run a spa in Nairobi and want a local rose water I can trust. I don't need bulk, but I need it consistent.
catchers.can: Supply small, tested batches, and ask Wanjiru, a spa owner and regular buyer, to introduce other spas.
catchers.confirm: Is your need tens of bottles with quality ahead of price, not hundreds of litres at the lowest cost?

catchers.hypo: I run a lab in Nairobi that screens plant material for pesticide residues, and I'd like small producers as clients.
catchers.can: Send small petal samples for screening and use the results to pick suppliers and build a supplier record.
catchers.confirm: Can you test a single small petal sample, not only commercial lots, at a price a micro-producer can pay?

catchers.hypo: My daughter is in Form 3 and struggling with chemistry. Do you tutor, or can you explain it to her?
catchers.can: Explain core ideas (acids and bases, separation, reaction types) in plain language, with kitchen or lab demonstrations when it fits.
catchers.confirm: Is she following a Kenyan secondary syllabus and needs concept help rather than exam-paper ghost-writing?

catchers.hypo: I'm setting up a small still for hydrosols and my condenser leaks. Can you tell me what to check?
catchers.can: Share what I've learned on gaskets, temperature control, cut points and quality checks, and point to where the failure usually is.
catchers.confirm: Is yours a small steam or water still, well under a few hundred litres, not an industrial plant?

catchers.hypo: I make soap and skincare by hand and my batches vary a lot. How do you keep quality steady?
catchers.can: Walk through my pH, colour and smell routine and help set up a basic batch log.
catchers.confirm: Do you make water-based or botanical products by hand in small batches, not at factory scale?

catchers.hypo: I'm writing school science material in Kikuyu and need a chemistry teacher to check that the concepts are correct.
catchers.can: Review the chemistry content and say where children actually get confused, based on sixteen years in the classroom.
catchers.confirm: Does the material need a chemistry reviewer for secondary-school learners, not only a translator?

forbids.text: I won't distil petals whose spraying history I don't know, whatever the price.
I won't sell a batch that fails my smell, colour or pH checks.
My still runs two days a week at most, so I can't take bulk or rush orders.
Weekends are for coaching my son's football team, so no weekend meetings or deliveries.
I can't make large upfront purchases or fund equipment out of my working capital.

projects.name: Clean-petal supply for rose water
projects.text: Build a dependable supply of roses with a known spray record so the still can run at full capacity and the waiting customers can be served.
roles_needed: rose grower with a spray log

policy.t1: If there's a real sign of fit, I'll share batch sizes, the quality problem with market roses, my still schedule and my QC method.
policy.t2: Once trust is high and the other party is clear, I'll share that money is tight when batches fail and that there is a family land dispute, in general terms only.
